decision: opened the single-boot design from Thomas's request on this fork
why: the installer only offers dual-boot today, and a wrong disk change can strand an Apple Silicon Mac

decision: Asahi v0.9.2 action_wipe repartitions a whole external disk and is hidden on the internal system disk
why: partitionDisk builds a new GPT and would remove the iBoot system container and System Recovery
evidence: asahi-installer v0.9.2 src/main.py action_wipe and src/diskutil.py partitionDisk

decision: the existing layout is ISC, macOS, Omarchy stub, EFI, boot, expanded root, System Recovery
why: removal already requires that order and grows macOS forward into space after it

decision: single-boot is a reclaim candidate that shrinks macOS to diskutil's MinimumSizePreferred and gives Omarchy the rest
why: that is every byte Apple will release while the Mac is booted from macOS; deleting the booted container is not safe

decision: reclaim is offered only when Apple_APFS_ISC is first, Apple_APFS_Recovery is last, and nothing else sits between them
why: a foreign partition after macOS would leave free space in front of Omarchy, and the root cannot grow backward

decision: the recovery account is mandatory for reclaim and cannot be deferred
why: it is the local volume owner on the Omarchy stub, created in paired recovery, and is the password that can still authorize startup changes after macOS is only as large as Apple allows

decision: dual-boot partition order stays as it is
why: shrinking macOS later opens a hole before the Omarchy group; moving those partitions was not tested on hardware and can strand the disk

decision: Python overlay tests passed, including reclaim admission and the refusal to resize an iBoot container
why: Linux can prove the planner and the recovery flag; it cannot boot a Mac

decision: rebuilt the engine twice from the omarchy.28 base and recorded the identical archive
why: the pin names the overlay inputs, so the archive digest has to follow them
